title: Tenant Pace Regulator for Continuous Batching and KV Offload
creator: Marina Chen
description: Design and implement a tenant-level pacing controller that enforces SLO budgets across continuous batching pipelines by inserting lightweight soft-yield checkpoints and coordinating KV-cache offload decisions to avoid GPU OOMs while preserving throughput.
background: Continuous batching improves GPU utilization but causes hard-to-control memory pressure from KV caches and long-running slices. Current preemption logic is coarse-grained: it either interrupts batches (causing latency cliffs) or defers work until strict memory reclamation triggers. We need a middle way that enforces latency SLOs, prevents OOM cascades, and maintains good throughput fairness across tenants.
proposed_solution: Introduce a Tenant Pace Regulator (TPR) that: 1) assigns soft-time-slices (micro-slices) per tenant derived from SLO budgets and recent tail-latency telemetry; 2) inserts soft-yield checkpoints at batch boundaries where KV working sets can be checkpointed to ephemeral host memory or compressed quantized offload; 3) applies a probabilistic KV-offload policy tuned by tenant urgency and predicted residency to avoid large synchronous evictions; and 4) exposes a control knob to route requests to lower-accuracy quantized variants when memory headroom is low.
design_details:
- Pace allocation: periodic credit assignment where credits ~= SLO_weight * recent_success_ratio.
- Soft-yield checkpoints: at natural micro-batch boundaries (end-of-chunk token emission) we attempt non-blocking KV spill to pagecache with a time budget (e.g., 5ms). If not completed, we record a deferred-spill hint.
- KV-offload scoring: score = alpha*recency + beta*frequency + gamma*(tenant_priority) + delta*(kv_size_ratio). Low-scoring entries are candidates for compressed offload or eviction.
- Probabilistic preemption: rather than hard interrupt, requests exceeding their time-slice are deprioritized (migrate to best-effort queue) and optionally routed to quantized variant.
- Safety: maintain a fast-path OOM watch that can still trigger immediate eviction if memory crosses critical watermark.
- Observability: new metrics per-tenant: pace_credits, soft_yield_count, kv_offload_bytes, quantized_reroutes, preempted_requests.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity vs gains: Adds orchestration complexity and more state per tenant; but reduces tail latency spikes and OOM incidents.
- Jitter: Soft-yielding can introduce micro-jitter (tens of ms) that may affect strict latency customers — mitigated via tenant SLO-weighted allocation.
- Offload cost: Host-side KV spilling/compression increases CPU and network I/O; tradeoff depends on workload locality.
- Accuracy: Routing to quantized models reduces quality for some requests; must be opt-in or tiered by SLA.
experiment_plan: 1) Simulation: run a cluster-level simulator with production trace (7 days) to validate credit allocator and offload policy. 2) Microbench: implement TPR prototype in runtime staging with single-GPU host to measure KV offload latency and credit cycling. 3) Canary: roll out to 1% traffic for low-tier tenants with aggressive monitoring. 4) Gradual ramp with auto-rollback on SLO regressions.
metrics_and_targets: P95 latency: <= baseline + 10ms for non-preempted tenants
P99 latency tail reduction: target 25% reduction compared to current preemptor
KV-related OOM incidents: reduce by 90% in canary group
